_readme: Waivers for check-docs.py, which reads this file from its own directory.
A section that genuinely does not apply to a repository should be ABSENT, not filled
with a placeholder - that is the first rule in standards/README-TEMPLATE.md. This file
is how you tell the checker so. Every waiver needs a reason: the reason is the point of
the file, because a waiver without one is indistinguishable from giving up.
app_folders  where to look for applications. Each immediate subdirectory holding a
project that declares <OutputType>Exe</OutputType> or WinExe counts as one
application, and the APPS-TABLE check wants each of them named in the
repository README. A class library does not count. A repository with no
executable projects yields none, so this is harmless in a C repository and
in a library repository whose src/ holds packages rather than programs.
waivers      a list. Each entry has:
files   paths relative to the repository root. A bare name such as
"README.md" also matches any path ending in it, so
"Desktop/README.md" waives one application's README.
checks  the check codes to waive for those files.
reason  why. Required. Write it for the next person.
Check codes: LINK ESCAPES ABSPATH MERMAID ALT-TEXT EMOJI-HEADING HAND-TOC
NEW-HEADING H1 BADGES NAVBAR INSTALL-ORDER LICENCE-LAST ABOUT STATUS
APPS-TABLE
The group-2 codes - H1 BADGES NAVBAR INSTALL-ORDER LICENCE-LAST ABOUT STATUS
APPS-TABLE - are only ever applied to the repository's own README.md. A per-application
README follows the shortened spine and has no badge row or nav bar of its own.
The waivers below are this repository's own.

waivers.reason: README style chosen by the owner (pcc-nd500 layout), 29-SEP-2026
